rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026)
rules.requirement: If your unit is covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, your landlord could raise rent by no more than 3% for the year July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Separately, the landlord may add an RSO surcharge of $1.61/month and a SCEP surcharge of $2.83/month, but only after registering the unit and giving you written notice.
rules.key_value: 3% (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026); plus $1.61/mo RSO and $2.83/mo SCEP surcharges

coverage.summary: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO). The page does not define which buildings are covered; it directs tenants to zimas.lacity.org or a text service to check RSO status.

rules.quoted_span:

is

rules.interaction: Page notes state law requires 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases under 10%. Non-RSO properties are directed to contact LAHD about allowable increases.
rules.conflict_note: The 3% figure is stated only for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, which ended before the query date 2026-10-01; the page (retrieved 2026-10-01) does not give the July 2026–June 2027 allowable increase. Code section not stated on the page.

rules.title: RSO: no additional percentage increase for utilities
rules.requirement: Starting February 2, 2026, a landlord of an RSO unit cannot add any extra percentage rent increase for utilities on top of the annual allowable increase.

coverage.summary: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.quoted_span: Beginning February 2, 2026, a landlord can no longer include any additional percentage increase for utilities.

notes: Official LAHD calculator page. It does not state the RSO code section or building coverage criteria, so citation is the ordinance name and coverage fields are left null. The stated 3% period ended June 30, 2026, before the query date, so the current figure needs verification. The page also mentions a state 30-day notice requirement for increases under 10%, but gives no citation; it was not extracted as a separate rule.
